data.title: Sector Update: Financial Stocks Higher Friday Afternoon
data.description:
01:41 PM EST, 11/13/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Financial stocks were advancing in Friday afternoon trading, with the NYSE Financial Index up 0.4% and the State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) adding 0.5%.

The Philadelphia Housing Index was up 0.1%, and the State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) was shedding 0.2%.

Bitcoin (BTC-USD) was falling 4.3% to $68,805, and the yield for 10-year US Treasuries was rising 9 basis points to 5.14%.

In economic news, the US Producer Price Index rose 0.3% in October, after a 1.4% increase in September and below the 0.4% gain expected in a Bloomberg-compiled poll. After excluding food and energy prices, core PPI increased 0.3%, as expected and following a 0.8% increase.

In sector news, OpenAI said Friday it is launching ChatGPT Wallet, which will allow the company's AI agents to make payments on users' behalf. The product was built in partnership with American Express (AXP), Mastercard (MA), and Visa (V), OpenAI said. ChatGPT Wallet will initially be available via its Dots AI agents for ChatGPT Pro users in the US, aged 18 and older, OpenAI said.

In corporate news, Barclays ( BCS ) plans to downsize its workforce by 200 positions across its investment bank starting next week, Bloomberg reported. Barclays ( BCS ) shares were down 0.2%.

Mizuho Financial ( MFG ) shares gained 1.7% after it posted higher fiscal H1 earnings and ordinary income.

Alexandria Real Estate Equities ( ARE ) will likely see growing earnings headwinds in 2027 and 2028 as better leasing activity is unlikely to offset near-term vacancies and tenant wind-downs, BofA Securities said in a note Friday. BofA downgraded the stock to underperform from neutral, and lowered its price target to $45 from $55. Alexandria shares were down 1.1%.

data.title: Update: Equities Fall Intraday as Nvidia Declines
data.description:
01:49 PM EST, 11/13/2026 (MT Newswires) -- (Updates with latest market prices and developments.)

US benchmark equity indexes were lower intraday amid a sell-off in Nvidia ( NVDA ) , while traders parsed the latest producer inflation report.

The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite was down 1.1% at 25,083.1 after midday Friday, while the S&P 500 fell 0.6% to 7,544. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged down 0.1% to 52,255. Among sectors, tech saw the steepest decline, while consumer staples paced the gainers.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) shares declined 2.9%, the second-biggest drop on the Dow, following a rating downgrade from Truist Securities.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) growth prospects could be constrained due to potential "know your customer" regulation following a controversy that led to Jensen Huang's ouster, Truist Securities said in a note e-mailed Friday.

Separately, Wedbush Securities said Nvidia ( NVDA ) is likely to exceed its fiscal third-quarter revenue estimates and issue a strong fourth-quarter outlook when it reports results next week.

Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) was the worst perform on the Dow, down 6.3% following the chipmaker's quarterly results. Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) tumbled 10%, the steepest decline on the S&P 500.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) said its services continued to recover across its infrastructure on Friday after a server issue triggered a global outage Thursday. The stock was up 0.3%.

US wholesale prices rose less than expected in October on a monthly basis, but annual growth hit the highest level in nearly four years, the government's producer price index report showed Friday.

Data released earlier this week showed a faster-than-expected increase in US consumer prices in October.

"An ongoing acceleration in inflation underscores the need for the (Federal Reserve) to remain focused on firming policy and taming the now dangerously elevated momentum in prices," Stifel said in a note on Friday.

Markets are pricing in a 90% probability that the Fed will lift rates by 25 basis points next month, compared with 86% on Thursday, according to the CME FedWatch tool. The remaining odds point to a hike by half a percentage point.

Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that raising interest rates is necessary to tame inflation, according to his interview with Bloomberg Television.

On Thursday, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said at a Yahoo Finance Invest conference that the central bank was at a "precarious moment" as inflation remained stubbornly high. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said that the Fed will likely need to raise rates further to tackle high inflation, according to a Reuters report.

Treasury yields were mixed intraday, with the 10-year rate rising four basis points to 5.14%, while the two-year rate was down 0.9 basis point to 4.86%

West Texas Intermediate crude oil was little changed at $88.76 a barrel in Friday afternoon trade, while Brent nudged up 0.2% to $95.99 a barre.

Spot gold ticked up 0.2% to $3,886.15 per troy ounce, while silver shed 2% to $49.08 per ounce.

data.title: PangeAI Partners with Sky Blue Impact to Accelerate Data Center Site Analysis with Agentic Geospatial AI
data.description:
Sky Blue Impact uses PangeAI's plain-English geospatial platform to assess grid, climate and hazard factors across potential data center locations, without lengthy consultant-led studies.

PALO ALTO, Calif., Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PangeAI, the agentic geospatial AI platform, announced that Sky Blue Impact has become a client, using PangeAI to support site analysis for data center development. The work focuses on helping Sky Blue's team evaluate and compare potential locations earlier and with greater confidence.

Agentic geospatial AI screens data center sites for grid access, water and climate risk in minutes, not weeks.

As demand for data centers continues to grow, choosing the right location has become one of the most consequential decisions developers make. Beyond land and cost, every candidate site must be evaluated for:

  • Grid capacity and proximity to existing infrastructure
  • Water availability for cooling
  • Climate and hazard exposure, including flooding, wildfire and extreme heat
  • Permitting and land-use constraints

Getting any one of these wrong can delay a project by years or add significant cost over the life of the facility. This analysis has traditionally meant lengthy studies from external GIS and engineering consultants, slowing down early-stage decisions and limiting how many options a team can realistically consider.

With PangeAI, Sky Blue Impact's team can ask site questions in plain English and receive decision-ready answers drawn from Earth-observation, climate and infrastructure data. PangeAI's autonomous geospatial analyst does the work a GIS specialist would normally do, gathering the relevant data, running the analysis and presenting the results in a form the team can act on. Questions that would typically take a consultant days or weeks to answer can be answered in minutes.

Because every site is assessed against the same criteria, the team gets a consistent view of risk and opportunity across all the locations it is considering. Answers come back with the underlying data and maps, so findings can be checked and shared with partners, investors or planning authorities.

"Data center siting is a high-stakes decision, and the teams making it shouldn't have to wait weeks for answers," said Johanna von der Leyen, CEO and co-founder of PangeAI. "We built PangeAI so that anyone on a development team can ask a question about a site and get a clear, evidence-based answer. Working with Sky Blue Impact shows how quickly that can change the way location decisions get made."

The collaboration reflects PangeAI's growing focus on data centers and energy infrastructure, sectors where location decisions carry long-term cost and resilience consequences. 

Organizations evaluating sites for data centers or energy projects can learn more and see how PangeAI works at pangeai.com.

About PangeAI

PangeAI is an agentic geospatial AI platform that turns location data into decision-ready answers. Teams with no GIS background ask questions in plain English, and PangeAI's autonomous geospatial analyst screens sites, assesses risk and monitors assets using Earth-observation and geospatial data, without replacing existing systems. PangeAI serves energy, data center, infrastructure and insurance organizations, with customers across USA, EU and Japan. Founded by Johanna von der Leyen (CEO) and Marek Miltner (CTO).

data.title: Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy at Purdue Launches the World's First Global Trusted Tech Standard (xGTT) with the Backing of Dozens of Visionary Leaders
data.description:
A free, open standard gives governments, businesses, universities and other decision-makers a common framework to assess whether companies operate in alignment with democratic values

WASHINGTON, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy at Purdue today announced the launch of the Global Trusted Tech Standard (xGTT), the world's first open standard for trusted technology. The principle behind xGTT is straightforward: trust must be earned through conduct. In democratic markets, companies earn trust by respecting the laws, rights, and principles that underpin free societies. The xGTT Standard provides governments, businesses, universities, and other institutions with a common, evidence-based framework for assessing whether a company has earned that trust.

Unlike standards that narrowly focus on technical performance, xGTT goes one step further, covering companies' compatibility with democratic values, such as respect for the rule of law, human rights, intellectual property, transparency, accountability, and others. xGTT applies to 15 critical and emerging technology (CET) sectors that are central to economic competitiveness, national security, and democratic resilience. Its criteria draw on the laws, regulations, standards, and established practices of 18 technologically advanced democracies, providing a shared reference point grounded in multiple jurisdictions rather than the position of any single government.

15 CETs covered by xGTT

18 Techno-Democracies Anchoring xGTT Criteria

1. Advanced Communications & Networking
2. Advanced Computing
3. Advanced Manufacturing & Materials
4. Artificial Intelligence
5. Autonomous Systems & Robotics
6. Biotechnology
7. Cybersecurity & Data Security
8. Directed Energy
9. Energy Technologies
10. Human-Machine Interfaces & Neurotech
11. Hypersonics
12. Positioning, Navigation & Timing
13. Quantum Technologies
14. Semiconductors & Microelectronics
15. Space Technologies

1. Australia
2. Canada
3. Denmark
4. Estonia
5. Finland
6. France
7. Germany
8. India
9. Israel
10. Japan
11. Netherlands
12. New Zealand
13. South Korea
14. Sweden
15. Switzerland
16. Taiwan
17. United Kingdom
18. United States 

The Global Trusted Tech Standard (xGTT) was announced at the Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy at Purdue's 2026 Trusted Tech Summit, the premier forum for Tech Diplomancy. The annual Summit brings together U.S. and allied government officials, technology executives, investors, and strategic partners to address the alliances, standards, and strategies shaping trusted technology. The launch of xGTT advances that mission by providing a shared, evidence-based framework for assessing corporate trustworthiness across critical and emerging technology sectors.

"Technology will either serve humanity or be used to undermine it, and trust is a decisive factor. By grounding economic collaboration in democratic principles, the Global Trusted Tech Standard makes it easier to operate efficiently in the free world, giving companies that earn trust a real competitive advantage," said Keith Krach, Chairman of the Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy at Purdue. "Together, we can ensure tomorrow's technology advances freedom for generations to come."

"Trust is the free world's superpower, and it is how we set the pace," said Michelle Giuda, CEO of the Krach Institute. "The Global Trusted Tech Standard delivers a real-world definition of trusted technology. It's simple, open, and free. Governments, companies, and universities can use it to guide procurement, supply chains, partnerships, and research, so collaboration moves faster and security and prosperity grow. That is how we win against those who weaponize technology against people."

xGTT Board of Governors

The xGTT Standard is guided by a Board of Governors, comprising 20 distinguished international experts spanning government, industry, academia, and civil society across 9 countries:

  • Audrey Tang, Chair of the xGTT Board; Taiwan's Cyber Ambassador-at-Large
  • Roberto Baldoni, former Deputy Director General of Italian Intelligence; founding Director General of Italy's National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN)
  • Isabel Cane, former Head of OECD Trust in Business and Blue Dot Network
  • Alex Capri, Senior Fellow and Lecturer, NUS Business School in Singapore
  • Dan DeLaurentis, Professor of Aeronautics and Astronautics and EVP for Research, Purdue University
  • Mike Derrios, Executive Director, Greg and Camille Baroni Center for Government Contracting, George Mason University
  • Rick Echevarria, Senior Vice President of Business Development, Keyfactor
  • Obiageli "Oby" Ezekwesili, former Nigerian Minister of Education and of Minerals; former World Bank Vice President for Africa
  • Fernando Garibay, GRAMMY® and BMI award-winning producer, songwriter, entrepreneur, author; Chairman and CEO, The Garibay Institute
  • Melanie Garson, Associate Professor in International Security, University College London
  • Dan Goldin, former Administrator, NASA
  • Yasmin Green, CEO, Jigsaw
  • Takashi Oda, Director of Business Strategy, NTT
  • Roman Pačka, Chief Advisor to the Director of the Czech National Cyber and Information Security Agency (NÚKIB)
  • Heather Petersen, former Head of Trust Strategy, DocuSign; former Executive Director, xDTM Standard Association
  • David Roberts, Executive Director, Li-Bridge
  • Harsh Shringla, Member of Parliament; former Indian Ambassador to the U.S.
  • Tom Sonderman, CEO, SkyWater Technology
  • Yigal Unna, former Director General, Israel's National Cyber Directorate
  • Ken Urquhart, Senior Fellow at the Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy at Purdue

The Board reviews the criteria on a standing basis, so the xGTT Standard adapts as the underlying technologies, and the risks they carry, continue to evolve. xGTT is guided by people who understand how real-world technology decisions are made. Their experience helps keep it relevant to the people and institutions that will use it.

How xGTT Works

The xGTT Standard contains 31 criteria for assessing a company's trustworthiness. These include 10 Red-Line Disqualifiers and 21 additional criteria covering Four Dimensions of Trust:

  • Democratic Government Trust: Whether democratic governments have trusted the company enough to contract with it, vet it, or invest in it.
  • Legal & Regulatory Compliance: Whether the company is free of serious misconduct findings by courts or governments that it has not remedied, such as corruption, fraud, repeated privacy violations, or intellectual property infringement.
  • Transparency & Disclosures: Whether the company's practices are open to independent verification, including audited financials, transparency about government requests for data, democratic supply chain practices, and published policies on corruption, human rights, and whistleblowers.
  • Technical Security Practices: Whether the company protects and manages its technology responsibly, from cybersecurity and secure software development to privacy, responsible AI, export controls, environmental compliance, and operational resilience.

A confirmed Red-Line failure disqualifies a company and ends the evaluation. For all other criteria, each applicable criterion receives a verdict of PASS, FAIL, UNCLEAR, or N/A, depending on the available evidence and whether the criterion applies. xGTT does not produce a single overall score or rank companies against one another.

Who xGTT is Designed For

xGTT helps a broad range of leaders make faster, evidence-based decisions about the trustworthiness of companies they may buy from, invest in, or partner with. Its criteria cover both technological excellence and democratic values, and each user applies them under its own authority and for its own purposes:

  • Governments and procurement authorities can integrate xGTT into procurement rules, requests for proposals (RFPs), and supply-chain vetting.
  • Defense forces can integrate it into military RFPs, procurement rules, and vetting of dual-use supply chains.
  • Enterprises and investors can apply it to enhance vendor due diligence, supply-chain risk assessment, and partnership decisions.
  • Industry associations and manufacturers can use it to demonstrate supplier trustworthiness, strengthen integration into global value chains, and expand access to trusted international markets.
  • Universities, research institutions, and standards bodies can use it as a reference for policy development, academic research, and coordination among like-minded institutions.

The xGTT Standard is for informational use only. It is not investment, legal, or financial advice, and xGTT evaluations do not constitute recommendations for or against any company, are not a regulatory finding or legal determination, and are not a substitute for independent due diligence. All decisions remain the responsibility of the organizations that use xGTT.

Government, Industry, and Civil Society Leaders Support the xGTT Standard

The Krach Institute already has endorsements from individuals all over the globe to include individuals from the Special Competitive Studies Project, Australian Strategic Policy Institute, Abba Eban Institute for Diplomacy and Foreign Relations, EDGE AI Foundation, Secure Economic Ecosystem, George Mason University's Baroni Center for Government Contracting, Keyfactor, Leonardo US Corporation, Jigsaw, U.S.-Taiwan Business Council, Mahindra Group, ReElement Africa, ADASA Inc., SEMI Americas, Opportunity International, Guidehouse, and TalentCraft. The standard also has the backing of representatives from the governments of the Czech Republic, Estonia, India, Israel, Italy, Panama, Romania, Taiwan and Ukraine, reflecting a growing commitment among democratic partners to advance trusted technology grounded in shared values.

Bi-khim Hsiao, Vice President of Taiwan:
"As a champion of trusted technology, Taiwan is proud to support a brighter future driven by the synergy of human and super intelligence, anchored by the xGTT Standard."

Luca Goretti, Chairman, Leonardo US Corporation:
"The Global Trusted Tech Standard (xGTT) builds trust by giving governments, companies, and partners a shared, verifiable benchmark for integrity, transparency, and security—reducing friction, enabling cross‑border collaboration, and accelerating the adoption of innovative technologies. If we all do not understand this simple statement and we do not work to implement it inside our regular and normal activities, within the institutions and industries, we have lost a great opportunity to build a strong and free society. We cannot afford to innovate only the technology, we have to innovate our mutual trust to be relevant…together!"

Yasmin Green, CEO, Jigsaw:
"At Jigsaw, we've learned that a secure internet requires not just new technology, but a new framework for trusted collaboration. The Global Trusted Tech Standard is that mechanism for enabling trusted partners to innovate together at speed and scale."

Mohit Kapoor, Group Chief Technology Officer, Mahindra Group:
"As technology becomes increasingly central to businesses and societies, trust must become as important as innovation itself. A common and transparent framework for security, responsible governance and technology trust can help enterprises build stronger partnerships and more resilient digital ecosystems. xGTT is a welcome step in that direction."

Audrey Tang, Taiwan's Cyber Ambassador-at-Large and xGTT Board Chair:
"The Global Trusted Tech Standard represents a strong step forward for our free and open societies. In cultivating decentralised, secure ecosystems, the standard aligns with the Taiwan Model, which employs civic technology and radical transparency to build collective trust. For Taiwan, digital security is more than a defensive barrier. It is an essential democratic practice. Embracing the standard advances global resilience and safeguards our shared digital commons against authoritarians, as well as proves that democracy delivers a safer, more collaborative future for all."

Eduardo Ortega-Barría, National Secretary for Science, Technology and Innovation, Panama:
"Panama commends the Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy for building the Global Trusted Tech Standard, a framework that turns shared values into verifiable practice. We endorse this initiative because trusted technology is precisely the foundation on which Panama is building itself as Latin America's trusted tech hub."

Pavlo Frolov, Co-Chair, Trusted Tech Caucus, Ukrainian Parliament:
"Ukraine understands better than most how technology shapes security, economic growth, and the defense of freedom itself. Even as Ukrainians courageously defend our nation, we are working with our democratic allies to build a trusted technology ecosystem for the next generation. The Ukrainian Trusted Tech Caucus is proud to endorse the Global Trusted Tech Standard and commends the Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy at Purdue for its leadership in accelerating the innovation and adoption of trusted technology."

Roberto Baldoni, Founding Director General, Italy's National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN):
"In today's fragmented geopolitical landscape, democratic nations must align on the development and adoption of disruptive technologies to safeguard Western leadership. The Global Trusted Tech Standard, launched by the Krach Institute, serves as a platform to unite free nations around shared principles of trust, transparency, and security. By fostering collaboration among governments, industry, and innovators, it empowers the private sectors of allied democracies to work together and thrive, ensuring that technological progress reinforces the stability of the free world."

Joe Stockunas, President, SEMI Americas:
"SEMI, the global trade association representing the semiconductor industry, recognizes the unprecedented pace of technological advancement shaping our sector. Ensuring these innovations are developed and deployed securely is essential to sustaining trust, resilience, and global collaboration. data.title: Nvidia's Huang turns to Paul Weiss, law firm that inked deal with Trump
data.description:
* Jensen Huang turned to New York firm amid ouster

* Paul Weiss faced Trump executive order before White House deal

* Leader Brad Karp resigned as chair over Epstein communications

By Mike Scarcella

WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang turned to law firm Paul Weiss amid his rapid fall this week, tapping a firm that reached a controversial deal with President Donald Trump last year and whose own longtime leader was forced to step down in February.

Huang resigned on Thursday after more than 30 years leading the top AI chipmaker, following reports that he had extramarital affairs with three women, including an Nvidia ( NVDA ) executive and Chinese businesswoman whom US intelligence suspects of being ​a Chinese spy.

Paul Weiss, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and a spokesperson for Huang had no immediate comment on Friday about the nature of the law firm's work for Huang.

New-York based Paul Weiss, with more than 1,500 lawyers, long has been a go-to for corporate boards and executives facing regulatory scrutiny, misconduct allegations or other reputational crises.

It built a reputation pairing lucrative work for Citigroup and other business clients with liberal advocacy and fundraising for Democratic candidates, including Kamala Harris.

But the firm drew sharp criticism within the legal profession and from Democrats last year after striking a deal with Trump to rescind an executive order the Republican president issued against it in March 2025.

Trump's order suspended security clearances for the firm's lawyers and restricted their access to government buildings and officials, citing its internal diversity policies and its association with a prosecutor who investigated the president.

Paul Weiss pledged in its settlement to dedicate $40 million in pro bono legal services to support "mutually agreed" projects with the White House, sparking similar deals by eight other law firms. Its longtime chairman Brad Karp defended the accord, calling Trump's order an existential threat.

The tumult facing Karp ramped up early this year, after emails surfaced showing Karp's extensive personal and business communications with the late convicted sex offender and financier Jeffrey Epstein.

Karp resigned from his leadership post in February, saying the reports about Epstein had created a distraction that was not in the firm's interests. He has not been accused of wrongdoing.

GO-TO FIRM FOR CORPORATE CRISES

Paul Weiss has a stable of former senior Justice Department officials and others who frequently step in for clients when crisis strikes.

BlackRock in 2021 hired partner Loretta Lynch, who was US Attorney General under President Barack Obama, to assist with an internal probe of former employees' claims of sexual harassment and discrimination.

Huang is working with Paul Weiss partners Melinda Haag and Walter Brown, the New York Times reported on Thursday. Haag served as US attorney in San Francisco during the Obama administration. She and Brown did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not independently confirm which lawyers at the firm are representing Huang.

The Republican leaders of several US House committees, including Foreign Affairs, addressed a letter to Brown on Thursday stating they wish to interview Huang in closed-door session next month.

Haag successfully defended former Fitbit executive Katherine Mogal, who was acquitted in 2020 of federal charges alleging theft of trade secrets from a rival wearable-device maker. Brown is on the team defending Meta Platforms in a lawsuit by an Australian mining magnate over scam ads on Facebook showing him promoting fake cryptocurrency.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board has hired another top firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Kratz to conduct an independent investigation. That probe will be led by Wachtell's Joon Kim, a former senior federal prosecutor in Manhattan.

(Reporting by Mike Scarcella; additional reporting by Alexandra Alper. Editing by David Bario and Nick Zieminski)

data.title: Fed likely to need to raise rates amid worsening inflation: Daly
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly said on Friday that her "bias" is that the central bank will need to increase its policy rate, particularly with services inflation moving in the wrong direction and some signs of inflation persistence.

"We're going to need to, in all likelihood, raise rates; I will deliberate this with my colleagues in December at our meeting and in all future meetings and make the collective decision that we judge is most appropriate for the economy that is evolving," Daly said at a University of Nevada, Las Vegas Center for Business and Economic Research forecast event. "Producers are telling us more and more that they're running out of room to take it out of margins, and they really want to consider passing along this to consumers. So that's the inflationary impulse we want to avoid." 

The core consumer price index, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, has risen about 0.3% month over month in each of the last three months. That's far higher than the 0.2% or less that would be consistent with year-over-year inflation at 2%, the Fed's target.

Daly, like several other policymakers, said she's particularly concerned that services inflation excluding housing is "not moving in the correct direction," which is particularly troubling because that slice of inflation tends to be sticky. 

"That's a place where you might think a retailer, or a professional business, if they have to buy more expensive IT goods, pay higher energy bills and have other inputs that are rising in price, maybe they're going to pass that along to customers," she said. 

The Fed raised its policy rate in September but held it steady in October, and financial markets are betting heavily on quarter-point interest-rate hikes at each of the Fed's December 8-9 and January 26-27 meetings. Daly said she feels markets understand how the Fed sets rates in response to economic conditions, without remarking specifically on the timing of coming rate hikes.

Daly said she is also paying close attention to consumer spending, which accounts for most of the US economy, as the December meeting approaches. 

"Consumer spending remains just surprisingly resilient; you just haven't seen a pullback, so I think that's the piece of information that I'm really looking for in the next one to two to three months: what happens in that, especially around the holiday season, do we see consumers giving up or do we see them keeping going even if prices rise?" Daly said. 

"Sitting here in Las Vegas...we're just starting to hear that the consumer may be running out of gas. And we're hearing that now in other states, not just Nevada."

(Reporting by Ann Saphir, Editing by Franklin Paul and Andrea Ricci )

data.title: Huang exit and US scrutiny imperil $3 billion in Chinese AI projects reliant on Nvidia
data.description:
BEIJING, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Nvidia ( NVDA ) has said US export controls have effectively shut it out of China's AI data-centre market, but a Reuters review has identified more than $3 billion in Chinese computing projects built around the American chipmaker's restricted processors.

The projects, stretching from China's wealthy coastal technology hubs to remote western provinces, reveal the scale of continuing demand for Nvidia ( NVDA ) hardware even as Washington seeks to curb Beijing's access to the technology powering the global artificial-intelligence boom.

The Reuters review examined more than 150 Chinese procurement notices, investment plans, construction contracts and corporate disclosures, identifying projects and equipment agreements with a combined reported value exceeding 23 billion yuan ($3.2 billion).

The findings paint a detailed picture of how deeply Nvidia ( NVDA ) technology remains embedded in China's AI expansion. They reveal the company's technology reaches well beyond China's largest tech firms, into local government-backed ventures, universities and regional computing centres.

The estimate includes planned investments and signed contracts as well as completed installations. It covers buildings, power systems and other infrastructure, and does not reflect spending on Nvidia ( NVDA ) chips alone.

China's commerce ministry and Nvidia ( NVDA ) did not immedietely respond to Reuters request for comment.

The findings come a day after Nvidia ( NVDA ) co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive amid a scandal over his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of intelligence ties to Beijing.

Huang, a vocal advocate of easing export restrictions, said last year Nvidia's ( NVDA ) market share in China had fallen from 95% to zero. The company has also excluded China data-centre computing revenue from its forecasts, citing regulatory uncertainty.

That does not mean Chinese demand has disappeared. While Nvidia's ( NVDA ) statements address its own ability to compete and sell directly in China, the documents Reuters reviewed show Chinese customers continuing to plan purchases and, in some cases, operating restricted processors.

Sunny Cheung, an analyst at the Washington-based Jamestown Foundation, said Reuters' findings reinforce his own view on enforcement: "Washington must stop focusing solely on who buys the chips on the surface and start examining who ultimately uses the computing power-and for what purpose." 

BILLIONS IN THE PIPELINE

Across China, developers and institutions are advancing billions of dollars in AI data-centre projects designed around restricted Nvidia H100, H200, and H800 processors. These range from massive regional computing hubs to retrofitted commercial sites - such as a facility in northwestern Gansu province that was expected to install thousands of Nvidia ( NVDA ) chips before year-end, though it remains unclear if those processors ever arrived.

While some facilities are already operational or under construction, operators are exposed to potential delays, supply disruptions, or costly redesigns around domestic chips as export controls tighten. 

Huang's departure could deepen these vulnerabilities by weakening Nvidia's ( NVDA ) lobbying leverage as US lawmakers press for tighter controls.

WASHINGTON'S DILEMMA

Washington began restricting Nvidia's ( NVDA ) advanced AI processors in 2022 and subsequently tightened controls on modified chips developed for China, including the H800.

In January, the Trump administration moved to review H200 export licences for eligible Chinese customers individually, subject to conditions.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) August filing said it was effectively excluded from China's data-centre computing market. But an IDC report cited by Reuters in October estimated Nvidia ( NVDA ) still accounted for 34% of Chinese AI-accelerator shipments in the first half of 2026.

The figures measure different things and do not establish how the restricted hardware identified in the Reuters investigation reached Chinese users.

The scrutiny has intensified since Huang's resignation on Thursday, following allegations involving Alice Huang, a former executive associated with Singapore-based Nvidia ( NVDA ) cloud partner Megaspeed.

Megaspeed has denied illegally diverting Nvidia ( NVDA ) chips to China. Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board launched an independent investigation, saying it had no reason to believe company secrets or US national security were compromised. There has been no public finding that Jensen Huang violated export-control laws.

The Chinese projects identified by Reuters have not been linked to Megaspeed or the allegations involving Huang.

data.title: Nvidia Faces Potential 'Know Your Customer' Regulation Following CEO Controversy, Truist Says
data.description:
01:39 PM EST, 11/13/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Nvidia's ( NVDA ) growth prospects could be constrained due to potential "know your customer" regulation following a controversy that led to Jensen Huang's ouster, Truist Securities said in a note e-mailed Friday.

Huang resigned as chief executive and a board member of the chipmaking giant Thursday following reports that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The technology bellwether named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO.

"It's not just about ex-CEO Jensen Huang's affairs or his resignation, but also about the potential that (Nvidia's ( NVDA )) culture becomes impaired, and that the company may have shipped (graphic processing units) that became accessible to companies and government entities in China, challenging future revenue performance," Truist Managing Director William Stein in the note to clients.

Huang's ties with an alleged intelligence asset for China likely emphasize the industry's lack of "know your customer," or KYC, rules, Truist said.

"We suspect US Department of Commerce may pursue KYC rules that could limit (Nvidia's ( NVDA )) revenue level and growth going forward," Stein said.

The brokerage said it would encourage the company's board to introduce mechanisms to make sure its AI products are used only by entities that are known by Nvidia ( NVDA ).

"We acknowledge this is a huge task that relies on significant new efforts by both (the company) and its customers," Stein said. "(Nvidia's ( NVDA )) leadership in this effort could be a redeeming outcome of this situation."

Truist downgraded its rating on the Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock to hold from buy and slashed its price target to $174 from $346.

The company's shares were down 2.8% in Friday afternoon trade, bringing its year-to-date losses to 13%.

Besides a possible regulatory backlash, Truist sees an end to what it called the "ride or die with Jensen" culture at Nvidia ( NVDA ).

"Huang's departure, and his association with a woman suspected of being an intelligence asset for China introduce new risks that significantly reduce our ability to reasonably forecast earnings and justify multiples," Stein said.

data.title: Dyania Health Brings Clinical Reasoning AI Inside the Hospital Firewall to Advance Patient Care with NVIDIA
data.description:
Dyania's Synapsis AI, which reasons through a patient's complete medical history, uses NVIDIA accelerated computing, so health systems can learn from their own records while keeping patient records within their walls.

JERSEY CITY, N.J., Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dyania Health today announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to put AI clinical reasoning to work inside health systems, on their own infrastructure, at the scale of their entire patient population. Dyania's Synapsis AI reads a patient's full medical record, across years of notes, operative reports, imaging reports and lab results, and answers clinical questions with evidence from the chart. NVIDIA accelerated computing makes it possible to do that across large patient populations behind the hospital firewall, without transferring patient records outside the health system. Together, the companies aim to give health systems the ability to learn from the full histories of the patients they have treated and turn that experience into earlier identification of care needs, more informed treatment decisions and better care for the next patient, while keeping those records within their own systems.

Turning clinical experience into better care

Health systems hold decades of clinical experience in their medical records, but much of it is difficult to analyze at scale. Much of the information that matters is in narrative text rather than structured fields, and interpreting it often requires manual review. Registries, outcomes studies and predictive models can be limited by how many charts a team can read by hand. Extracting and interpreting the clinical information needed to build them remains a major bottleneck.

Synapsis AI performs that reasoning. It is built to work the way a specialist works through a chart: longitudinally, across every document, resolving what a patient actually had, when, and with what evidence. Doing this for one patient is a reasoning problem. Doing it for an entire health system, continuously, inside the hospital's own environment, requires substantial computing capacity. Dyania brings the clinical reasoning engine and implementation experience; NVIDIA brings the accelerated computing platform and the software that lets it run securely and efficiently on premises.

Synapsis AI is built on the NVIDIA AI Enterprise software stack end to end. Dyania trains its proprietary clinical models with the NVIDIA NeMo framework for model training and reinforcement learning. Inside the health system, Synapsis AI runs on NVIDIA TensorRT and TensorRT-LLM on the hospital's own NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure, so inference stays inside the hospital's private network.

Under the collaboration, the companies will work to bring Synapsis AI on NVIDIA infrastructure to health systems in the U.S. and internationally, publish joint case studies, and integrate Synapsis AI with NVIDIA's healthcare software stack. Areas the companies are evaluating include NVIDIA Confidential Computing for training and inference, NVIDIA Dynamo for distributed inference serving, Multi-Instance GPU for partitioning GPUs across concurrent clinical workloads, and scaling to many NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs as deployments move from batch processing toward near-real-time clinical insight at the point of care.

"The opportunity for AI in healthcare is to give care teams more time and insight to focus on patients," said Chelsea Sumner, Healthcare AI Startups Ecosystem Lead at NVIDIA. "Dyania Health brings deep clinical expertise to that opportunity, using NVIDIA's AI platform to support research, help identify gaps in care and build a more complete understanding of patients' needs."

"This is a watershed moment for patient care. Every patient's story is spread across years of notes, reports and results, and for the first time we can reason across all of it at once, the way a specialist does, for every patient in a health system rather than one chart at a time," said Eirini Schlosser, founder and CEO of Dyania Health. "Synapsis AI reads the full record, draws the clinical conclusions and shows the evidence behind them, and NVIDIA gives us the computing power to do that inside the hospital, with every record staying where it belongs. What we have shown with Cleveland Clinic is that a health system can learn from the patients it has already treated to give the next patient the right care sooner."

Predicting how long replacement heart valves will last

The first work from the collaboration is a Cleveland Clinic study of 7,812 patients who received an aortic valve replacement between 2005 and 2021. The study addressed a central concern for patients: How long will the replacement valve last, and will another procedure be needed? To answer this, researchers reviewed up to 16 years of patient care, most of it in narrative notes and echocardiogram reports that can be challenging to capture in registries.

Running on NVIDIA accelerated computing inside Cleveland Clinic's environment, Synapsis AI identified the patient population and answered 88 clinical questions for each patient, covering the valve and its characteristics, co-existing conditions, laboratory trends, medications, follow-up ultrasound measurements and later clinical events. The study produced a detailed clinical dataset in far less time than a manual review would take. Additionally, a predictive machine-learning model was trained that is capable of predicting valve failure and reintervention risk timelines for every patient.

The model found that the type of valve implanted was the strongest determinant of how quickly it deteriorated, while age and other medical conditions shaped whether and when a second procedure was performed. The analysis also examined how follow-up information, such as heart ultrasounds following surgery, can substantially raise predictive accuracy around future interventions. The model estimates an individual patient's risk at three, five and 10 years and revises the outlook with each new ultrasound. The tool is used to help inform care but requires external validation from clinicians. 

"Using technology to bring together and analyze information that can help us predict the duration of implanted heart valves is a promising step towards enhanced outcomes and more personalized care for patients," said Lars G. Svensson, MD, PhD, Chief, Heart, Vascular & Thoracic Institute at Cleveland Clinic.

The heart valve study illustrates the broader potential of the collaboration. The same technology could help health systems learn from their own experience to understand which patients would benefit from certain therapies, which treatments hold up over time, and why outcomes differ between patients who look alike on paper. Looking ahead, Synapsis AI agents will continuously train predictive models of this kind, so that recommendations for the next recommended action in a patient's care keeps improving in accuracy as precision medicine advances.

About Dyania Health
Dyania Health exists so that no patient is missed because the answer was buried in their chart. Its clinical reasoning engine, Synapsis AI, reads a patient's entire medical history, across years of notes, reports and results, and answers clinical questions with the evidence to back them, so care teams can see which patients need attention, which treatments are working and what should happen next. It does this for every patient in a health system, inside the hospital firewall, with no record ever leaving. Health systems use Synapsis AI to find patients who need care they have not yet received, strengthen registries and quality programs, and turn their own clinical experience into better outcomes for the next patient. Dyania Health is headquartered in Jersey City, New Jersey.

data.title: Hours-long Microsoft outage disrupts businesses, governments globally
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - A more than 12-hour outage of Microsoft Outlook and Teams crippled communications for businesses and governments globally on Friday, forcing some organizations to revert to fax machines and halting at least one bond repurchase in Europe.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) said server issues were behind the incident that also affected its Copilot AI assistant and that a broader roll-out of software fixes was starting to stabilize the system. It said it was not aware of any malicious activity.

Outlook and Teams are two of the most widely used workplace applications with hundreds of millions of users. The outage prevented people from performing essential functions such as sending emails, managing calendars and hosting virtual meetings.

It affected government agencies from Australia to Japan and the United States, caused delays at trading firms, hindered some companies from publishing earnings and prompted airlines to warn customers of communication lags, according to public statements.

Organizations that host Microsoft ( MSFT ) services on their own servers, rather than in the cloud, were somewhat spared.

ANOTHER OUTAGE FOR MICROSOFT

The outage is one of the longest in Microsoft's ( MSFT ) history and the second disruption to its services this year.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) said the outage specifically hit features tied to Exchange Online - its cloud-based email and scheduling hub - leaving unconnected applications operational.

The incident deepens questions about the global reliance on a handful of Big Tech companies that supply both the essential software and the cloud infrastructure that underpins it.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) shares were down 0.4% in early trading. They have gained roughly 8% so far this year.

Disruptions and financial losses from the outage could result in numerous insurance claims, but the overall hit to insurers is expected to be limited, said Mario De Cicco, vice president of European financial institutions at Morningstar DBRS.

De Cicco estimated global insured losses from the incident at between $300 million and $500 million, well below the $400 million to $1.5 billion financial toll from the 2024 CrowdStrike outage that crashed more than 8 million Windows-based computers and caused widespread disruptions.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) also faced an outage with its 365 services in January this year and in October last year. Last month, it reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted its suite of productivity software, and a range of industries worldwide. 

"The bigger worry is that this is not the first Microsoft ( MSFT ) 365 outage this year," said Josh Gilbert, a market analyst at trading platform eToro.

"If reliability starts to look like a recurring problem, it hands every IT department a reason to think twice before putting even more of their business in one provider's hands."

Still, some analysts have questioned whether such incidents can push customers on to rivals due to the steep switching costs of replacing tools embedded so deeply in daily operations.

TRADES HAD TO BE CONFIRMED BY FAX

A spokesperson for the UK government said it was working with Microsoft ( MSFT ) to find a solution for the outage that hit organizations such as the NHS and London's Metropolitan Police.

Lack of access emails and other services was impacting the Metropolitan Police's ability to report some crimes online, though its ability to respond to calls was not affected.

NHS said its local services were turning to alternate measures such as using IT systems or paper records.

For businesses, the fallout was widespread.

European exchange operator Euronext reported email disruptions, British insurer Aviva activated backups for its earnings calls and Danish shipping giant Maersk warned customers of delayed updates.

American AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic also faced issues with Microsoft ( MSFT ) connectors, while Indian airlines IndiGo, Akasa Air and Air India said their email support services were impacted.

The outage also disrupted fund management at Taiwanese securities firms, life insurers, and investment trust companies. One of the companies went as far as cancelling a bond repurchase transaction, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters.

Another Taiwanese financial company resorted to using fax to confirm trades, a second source said.

In the US, electric truck maker Workhorse Group rescheduled its results on Thursday to November 16, while Switzerland's Richemont briefly delayed its first-half results announcement on Friday.  

In Australia, where the spy agency and federal police were among organizations caught in the outage, Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke said Microsoft ( MSFT ) does not suspect a cyber attack.

"The impact that they are dealing with ... is very much on email systems," the minister added.

data.title: Egan-Jones Examines How Falling Development Costs Could Reshape Video Games
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Egan-Jones released a commentary examining why Grand Theft Auto VI, due November 19, may mark the end of an era of expensive video game development. The piece finds that artificial intelligence has cut the capital needed to develop and port games, and offers investors a framework for the shift.

Video games are a business of about $200 billion a year, six times the box office, and 85% of US teens play them, according to the commentary. Outside estimates put development of Grand Theft Auto VI at $1.0 billion to $1.5 billion, or $1.5 billion to $2.0 billion including marketing. Its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, earned about 30 times what it cost.

Egan-Jones believes owners of well-recognized intellectual property hold a major advantage, because familiar franchises can make marketing investment more successful. With development costs falling, these owners can open their franchises to anyone, license them broadly for a fee or royalty, or develop them in-house or with accountable partners. Egan-Jones expects owners most sensitive to tainting, such as Disney, to favor self-development or close partnerships.

For credit investors, the commentary describes a significant shift. Rather than funding a few large projects and studios, lenders may begin financing many smaller ones, which offers diversification but calls for more due diligence. Egan-Jones also expects growing demand to finance marketing, which it describes as generally safer than financing development because creditors sidestep the risk of "development hell."

The commentary also points to pressure on established players. Developers such as BioWare and Ubisoft have closed or significantly reduced operations, and Egan-Jones writes that Microsoft's studio acquisitions may have been poor investments given the shift in costs. It adds that platforms controlling product discovery should continue to benefit: players spent about $82 billion on mobile games through the App Store and Google Play in 2025, and Steam reached a record 43.5 million concurrent users on October 11.

Egan-Jones concludes that Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to be one of the largest launches in entertainment history and may still be the last of its kind. For lenders, the new model needs less financing over the long term.

data.description:

* Euro zone third-quarter GDP grows 0.4% quarter-on-quarter

By Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair, Johann M Cherian and Avinash P

Nov 13 (Reuters) - European shares were little changed on Friday, but recorded their best week since late June as strong earnings and a rotation out of tech globally helped investors look past geopolitical risks and the volatility involving AI stocks.

The STOXX 600 closed flat at 664.14 points, and gained over 2% for the week. Heavyweight Euro STOXX banks index rose over 4% this week and led broader gains.

Robust earnings, along with a fall in oil prices on hopes of a potential easing of the US-Iran conflict earlier this week, helped the STOXX 600 breach record-high levels for the first time since August on Thursday.

Analysts also pointed to structural tailwinds that could boost Europe's prospects in the long term.

"Europe is building its rearmament program, its industrial program, strategic autonomy, its energy infrastructure and its defence," said Jitania Kandhari, deputy CIO, Solutions & Multi-Assets at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

"That is trickling into different pockets of the economy and the markets now. When investment in capex picks up, it has spillover effects," she said.

Mirroring the optimism, Goldman Sachs raised its 12-month target for the STOXX 600 to 700 points from 695.

TECH LOSES STEAM

On Friday, the tech sector fell 1.3%, leading losses.

Uncertainty over the outlook for the AI trade rippled through global markets following Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO, as investors fretted about the future of the AI goliath that has underpinned much of the rally in global markets.

Chip stocks such as Infineon and Aixtron were down more than 4% each, while AI equipment makers such as Schneider Electric and Legrand were also lower.

Adding to caution, crude prices swung in the session as Washington's focus on blockading Iran and ramping up other economic pressures allayed fears of renewed direct conflict in the Middle East.

Investors also weighed some corporate earnings on Friday.

Wise Group gained 7.7% to top the benchmark index after the money transfer company reported a 23% net revenue rise in the first half of its fiscal year.

In contrast, Richemont fell 3.8% after the Cartier owner reported weaker-than-expected sales in its jewellery unit during the second quarter.

Acciona fell 8%, languishing at the bottom of the index after subsidiary Acciona Energia said it would not meet its €2 billion ($2.21 billion) target for its asset rotation programme.

On the data front, the euro zone economy grew by 0.4% quarter-on-quarter in the third quarter, according to a flash gross domestic product estimate from the EU's statistics agency.

data.title: Neoclouds, AI stocks slide again as Nvidia turmoil rattles sector
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - Shares of AI-related US companies dropped again on Friday, with neoclouds among the worst hit, fueled by fresh jitters over AI financing following Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt exit.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 declined 2%, on pace to erase about $800 billion in market value if the losses hold through the close. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index also shed 5.1%, facing a more than $560 billion wipeout for the day.

CoreWeave and Nebius Group, neocloud firms backed by Nvidia ( NVDA ), slumped 8.8% and 9%, respectively, extending their sharp declines from Thursday when longtime CEO Huang stepped down after revelations of extramarital affairs.

Nvidia ( NVDA ), under Huang, has financed infrastructure built around its chips, a strategy that has driven demand but also raised questions about circular funding flows between the chipmaker and its customers.

"It's a short-term death blow to the industry because the amount of vendor financing and financing guarantees that Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Jensen Huang stepped into are now over," said Thomas Hayes, chairman of Great Hill Capital LLC.

Further, Nscale, a British cloud provider also backed by Nvidia ( NVDA ), amended its IPO filing to say it expects to report a net loss of $1.7 billion in the nine months ended September 30, wider than the $433.3 million net loss a year ago.

A media report on Friday said Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Huang. Arm shares were last down 4.8%.

Chip stocks, widely regarded as among the biggest winners of the AI boom, also dropped. Advanced Micro Devices fell 10.7% and Broadcom lost 5.9% after both gained for the last five sessions.

Memory chipmaker Micron Technology shed 5% while data storage companies Western Digital and Sandisk dipped 6.6% and 8.1%, respectively.

Photonic product makers Lumentum and Coherent, along with AI server makers Dell and HPE, fell between 5.3% and 9% each.

Utilities and equipment suppliers exposed to the AI boom, including GE Vernova, Constellation Energy and Vistra, eased about 2.2% to 3.5% each.

AI hyperscalers were also mostly lower, barring Meta Platforms, which rose 1.2%. Oracle, Alphabet, Amazon.com and Microsoft fell between 0.2% and 2.7%.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) quarterly earnings and AI lab Anthropic's much-awaited public markets debut are set for next week and could prove to be catalysts for sentiment towards AI.

"You have no idea what to expect from Nvidia ( NVDA ). That's the problem. This company is pure uncertainty right now," said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers.

Funding will advance the commercialization of logical-qubit quantum computers and strengthen U.S. leadership in quantum technology.

BOULDER, Colo.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Atom Computing, a leader in scalable neutral-atom quantum computing, today announced it has signed an agreement for up to $100 million with the U.S. Department of Commerce to accelerate research and development of fault-tolerant, utility-scale quantum computers. The award follows a Letter of Intent announced earlier this year and represents a significant investment in advancing next-generation computing technologies critical to U.S. economic competitiveness, scientific leadership, and national security.

Atom Computing's neutral-atom architecture is increasingly recognized as one of the most viable approaches for building large-scale, commercially useful quantum computers. Today’s announcement closely follows the company’s recent selection as the only neutral atom company to advance to Stage C of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (DARPA QBI) with potential funding up to $300 million.

Atom has consistently demonstrated technical leadership through several industry milestones, including being the first to build a platform with more than 1,000 qubits, the first neutral-atom company to demonstrate sub-threshold behavior on a system with full, end-to-end quantum error correction over many rounds, and the first to commercially offer a logical-qubit quantum computer. In 2025 Atom Computing sold its first commercial on-premises quantum computer to QuNorth, a Nordic quantum initiative funded by EIFO and Novo Nordisk Foundation.

"Quantum computing is reaching a critical inflection point where scientific breakthroughs must rapidly translate into commercial reality," said Dr. Ben Bloom, CEO and Founder of Atom Computing. "This $100 million contract enables us to aggressively scale the engineering required to bring fault-tolerant quantum computing to market and ensure the United States leads the transition into the utility-scale era."

The Department of Commerce contract will accelerate several of Atom Computing’s strategic R&D initiatives which will shorten the timeline to economically viable quantum computing, including:

  • Developing critical technologies in-house to improve system performance, reliability, and vertical integration
  • Expanding parallel engineering and testbed infrastructure to rapidly validate innovations and speed product development
  • Strengthening R&D collaboration with key supply chain partners to support manufacturing scale-up and long-term growth

Industry and government interest in practical quantum computing continues to accelerate, with advances in error correction, system scale, and hardware performance driving increased confidence in the technology's commercial potential. Atom Computing has demonstrated leadership in logical-qubit systems and fault-tolerant architectures, translating scientific breakthroughs into deployable commercial systems for real-world applications.

Atom Computing is developing large-scale quantum computers to enable companies and researchers to achieve unprecedented computational breakthroughs. Utilizing highly scalable arrays of optically trapped neutral atoms, the company has developed systems with over 1,000 qubits, featuring advanced capabilities towards fault-tolerant quantum computing. data.title: European Stocks Close Mixed in Friday Trading; EU, Euro Area GDP Growth in Line With Projections
data.description:
11:51 AM EST, 11/13/2026 (MT Newswires) -- European stock markets closed mixed in Friday trading as the European Union and Euro area reported monthly and annual GDP growth that was in line with analyst forecasts.

The Stoxx Europe was off 0.1%, Germany's DAX declined 0.1%, the FTSE 100 rose 0.4%, France's CAC gained 0.1%, and the Swiss Market Index fell 0.3%.

Seasonally adjusted GDP increased by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU in Q3, compared with the previous quarter, according to a flash estimate published by Eurostat, the statistical office of the EU. Compared with a year earlier, seasonally adjusted GDP increased by 1.3% in the euro area and 1.5% in the EU.

Both readings met expectations by analysts polled by Bloomberg.

Eurostat also reported that the number of employed remained unchanged in both the euro area and the EU in Q3, compared with the previous quarter. Compared with a year earlier, employment increased 0.4% in both the euro area and the EU.

In corporate news, Novo Nordisk said Friday it submitted etavopivat, a once-daily oral treatment for sickle cell disease in patients 12 and older, for approval with the US Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency.

A phase 3 trial showed the drug cut vaso-occlusive crises by 27% and delayed the first crisis by about four months versus placebo, the company said.

The FDA and European regulators are expected to decide on the applications in 2027, and etavopivat holds orphan and fast track designations, Novo Nordisk said.

Shares of the Danish pharmaceutical company rose 1% in Copenhagen.

AstraZeneca's Baxfendy, developed for the treatment of adults with insufficiently controlled hypertension, has been recommended for marketing authorization by the European Medicines Agency's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use, the agency said Friday.

The health agency said the recommendation is based on clinical trials showing statistically significant reductions in systolic and diastolic blood pressure compared with placebo in patients whose hypertension remained uncontrolled despite treatment with at least two medications.

The European Commission will make the final decision on marketing authorization, the agency said.

Shares of AstraZeneca increased 0.6% in London.

A French judge has ordered Hermes heir Nicolas Puech to undergo a cognitive assessment, Reuters reported Friday, citing two people with direct knowledge of the decision. Puech is suing the company, alleging he was cheated out of his 6% stake in the luxury goods giant.

Hermes didn't immediately respond to a request for comment from MT Newswires.

Shares of Hermes were 0.1% lower in Paris.

Nokia said Friday its Federal Solutions unit won a US Department of Defense contract to build systems using 5G and 6G networks to detect and track objects for threat awareness.

The project, known as Real-World Application Prototyping for ISAC Demonstration, combines multiple sensing methods on Nokia's AI-RAN platform to identify unmanned aircraft threats, the company said.

Texas Tech University, DeepSig, Hidden Level and Future Technologies are among subcontractors supporting the project, Nokia said.

Shares of Nokia rose 1% in Olso.

Novartis' Cosentyx was recommended for expanded use to treat adolescents aged 12 and older with moderate-to-severe hidradenitis suppurativa, a chronic skin condition that causes painful lumps and inflammation, the European Medicines Agency said Friday.

The recommendation covers adolescents who have not responded adequately to standard systemic treatments for the condition, the agency said.

The European Commission will make the final decision on the proposed change to the drug's marketing authorization, it added.

Shares of the Swiss pharmaceutical company edged 0.1% higher in Zurich.

GSK's Bexsero received a recommendation from the European Medicines Agency to immunize newborns against meningococcal disease, the regulator said Friday.

The EMA's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended the vaccine for meningococcal disease caused by Neisseria meningitidis group B in children from 6 weeks of age and older, compared with two months and older previously, the regulator said.

Shares of GSK gained 0.7% in London.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.
